newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - April 30.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - April 30.

text.p: NEW YORK - U.S. blue chips pushed to fresh session highs in late trading on Tuesday in a broad rally following favorable econommic data.
The Dow was up 165 points, or 2.5 percent, at 6949.6 at 7.35 a.m. NZT. Gainers held a lead of almost four-to-one over decliners.
The Dow pushed through the 6900 mark, which some technical analysts pointed to as key near-term resistance.
Traders also cited the move by the long-bond below the seven percent yield mark as a bullish sign. The 30-year Treasury bond was up 1-16/32 to yield 6.99 percent.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index closed at its highest level for six-weeks, encouraged by sharp gains in New York after U.S. economic data showed inflationary pressures to be easing, calming fears of a near-term interest rate rise. The leading index added 43.5 points or 0.99 percent to close at 4,433.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade up 0.60 percent, slightly off the day's highs, as the market continues to enjoy the support of the stronger dollar, firmer overnight close on Wall Street underpinned trade, resistance seen at 3,400 points, but scepticism about viability of upturn may limit the advance. The DAX index closed bourse trade at 3,383.19 up 20.13
points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,425.86.

PARIS - The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 52.61 points or 2.06 percent to 2,602.86, traders said the market strengthened on the back of market-friendly U.S. data which appeared to lower the risk of an interest rate rise by the Fed next month.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher, hitting a record closing high after the U.S. employment cost index report led to a sharp rise in late trade, first quarter data, which is considered an important indicator of U.S. inflation trends, was favourable for the markets, gains in government bond futures and positive corporate news also helped
shares. The Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 33.39 points or 1.1 percent to 3,070.95.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market was closed today for a National Holiday and will reopen on Wednesday.
On Monday, the key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 57.51 points or 0.31 percent at 18,670.37, after hovering within a limited range throughout the session.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended on a soft note amid heavy profit-taking in China-related plays following their recent surge and caution ahead of U.S. economic data due later. The Hang Seng blue-chip index closed 9.75 points or 0.08 percent

SYDNEY - Investor enthusiasm over the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's plan to revamp its steel division helped drive Australian shares to their highest close in over two months, brokers said BHP's plan to shut down steel production at its Newcastle plant, BHP's oldest, by 1999 was well-received and had buoyed the market overall. The key All Ordinaries Index closed up 17.4 points at 2,479.1, its highest close since February 27.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended strong with volumes at a record high boosted by a massive trade in NBS Holdings Ltd during the afternoon, "The talk of the day has been the NBS transaction," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollak told Reuters. The Industrial index ended up 45.4 points to 8,451.4, the All-share index added 34.4 points to 7,106.4 and the Gold index ended down 29.8 points to 1,205.2.
